results.note: Rendered p. 7, §6.1 paragraphs 1-3 match: 'toxicological nightmare' 35 years ago; links to variables often absent; drug properties only part. Ferner analysed Leikin & Watson's published ratios for several drugs. QSAR suggests ionisation of basic drugs contributes. Role fits.

results.corrected_extracted: In human bodies sampled more than once, significant falls in femoral blood after death were reported for THC (one study, ref 30) among other substances; no sizes are given. Separately, where the interval was reported or estimated, the first sample came on average 17 h after death (range 1–292 h), pooled from 12 references that do not include the THC study.
results.note: Rendered p. 6, §5.1 paragraph 3: THC fall and 17 h (1-292) confirmed. The mean covers only intervals 'available or estimated', and its 12 cited references exclude ref 30, so it should not be read as the THC study's interval.
